papers.title_in_file: Zeno Blockade Enabling Photonic Quantum Optimization
papers.version_note: arXiv:2604.13032v1 (14 Apr 2026); the text matches the record.
papers.what_it_is: A theoretical and simulation proposal from Quantum Computing Inc for an all optical Zeno blockade annealer that solves (weighted) maximum independent set using sum frequency generation or two photon absorption.

assertions.value: The authors state that they explore the potential of implementing an optical quantum optimizer using non-linear optics, specifically sum-frequency generation and/or two photon absorption, with Zeno effects enforcing independence constraints and a linear protocol finding a maximum independent set.
quotes: In this work we explore the potential of implementing an optical quantum optimizer using non-linear optics, specifically using sum-frequency generation and/or two photon absorption.
This proposal uses Zeno effects to enforce independence constraints and then a linear protocol to find a maximum independent set
assertions.certainty_reason: The abstract states the paper's own scope.

assertions.value: The abstract states that the authors numerically study the effect of coherent versus incoherent incarnations of the Zeno effect, finding superior performance from the latter.
quotes: We numerically study aspects of the protocol, including the effect of coherent versus incoherent incarnations of the Zeno effect, finding superior performance from the latter.
assertions.certainty_reason: An abstract statement; the body results are in assertions on Sections 5.1 and 5.2.
assertions.reader_inference: The body (Sections 5.1, 5.2 and 7) reports better performance from the coherent Zeno effect, so the word 'latter' in the abstract reads as a slip: it conflicts with the body if it means the incoherent case.

assertions.value: The authors state that photon loss error only leads to a smaller set, never a larger one, and propose taking multiple copies of the problem with fully connected bipartite edges between copies and decoding a vertex as in the set if it is in the set in one or more copies, with a full analysis beyond the scope of the paper.

assertions.value: The authors state that they study the dynamics of solving small maximum independent set problems: a three node line graph whose unique maximum independent set is {0, 2}, and a five node graph whose maximum independent set is {0, 3, 4}.
quotes: For the purpose of this paper we will study the dynamics of solving small maximum independent set problems.
it can easily be shown that the set s = {0, 2} is the unique maximum independent set on this graph.

assertions.reader_inference: All numerical results rest on these two tiny graphs and a two node weighted example; the paper reports no scaling study.

assertions.value: The authors state that the maximum independent set problem and its weighted variant are known to be NP hard, with a simple one to one reduction to set packing, one of Karp's original 21 NP complete problems.
quotes: The maximum independent set problem and by extension the weighted variant is known to be NP-hard, in fact it can be mapped in a simple one-to-one reduction to set packing[44], one of Karp’s [45] original 21 NP-complete problems.
assertions.reader_inference: Standard complexity result attributed to prior work.

assertions.value: The authors state that, from general graph theoretical arguments, the number of qubits in a quasi 2D arrangement needed to map a highly connected problem must be the square of the number of original variables.
quotes: From general graph-theoretical arguments, the number of qubits in a quasi-2D arrangement to map a highly connected problem must be the square of the number of original variables.

assertions.value: The authors state that a key advantage of their optical protocol is that it naturally allows arbitrary connectivity, thereby avoiding overheads from problem mappings.
quotes: One of the key advantages of the optical protocol we propose here is that it naturally allows arbitrary connectivity, and thus avoids overheads from problem mappings.
assertions.reader_inference: Connectivity in the time bin design needs delay and switch networks (Section 4.2, Appendix C) and fast switching; no hardware or resource count is given.

assertions.value: The authors state that the work sets entropy computing apart from coherent Ising machines by presenting a theoretical implementation of entropy computing which is unambiguously fully quantum, an analog of which does not exist for coherent Ising machines.

assertions.reader_inference: The authors are at the company that builds entropy computing hardware; the claim concerns a theoretical protocol, not that hardware.

assertions.value: The authors state that it has been shown that loss based Zeno effects can lead to a theoretical quantum advantage on unstructured search, yielding an analog equivalent of the speedup from Grover's algorithm.
